questions.q: Why does this Conditional Access policy start as a pilot instead of a tenant-wide rollout?
options: Pilots are required by Microsoft licensing
A misconfigured policy applied tenant-wide on day one could lock out everyone at once; a pilot limits the blast radius
Tenant-wide rollout isn't technically possible
Pilots are cheaper than tenant-wide policies
questions.explain: Scoping to a small group first limits any mistake's impact to people who understand what's happening and can report a problem immediately.

questions.q: Who does the pilot policy's "Users and groups" assignment target?
options: Every employee at Hartwell
Only the CA-Pilot-SOC-IT security group -- IT and Security team members
Only Owen Mercer and Renee Castellano
Only the break-glass account
questions.explain: The pilot is scoped to the CA-Pilot-SOC-IT group, not rolled out to everyone at Hartwell.

questions.q: What two controls does the pilot policy require for a sign-in?
options: A VPN connection and a specific browser
Multi-factor authentication and a compliant device
A strong password and nothing else
Approval from the IT Director for every sign-in
questions.explain: The policy requires MFA and a compliant device, so neither a stolen password alone nor a non-compliant device alone is enough.

questions.q: Why is the break-glass account excluded from the policy on day one, rather than added later?
options: It doesn't matter when it's excluded
A misconfigured policy or outage could lock out every administrator simultaneously if the break-glass account isn't excluded from the start
Break-glass accounts aren't allowed to be excluded
Because Owen asked for it to be excluded later
questions.explain: Adding the exclusion after a lockout is a much worse way to learn why break-glass accounts exist -- it has to be in place before the policy is ever turned on.

questions.q: What happens during report-only mode, before the policy is enforced?
options: Nothing is evaluated at all
Entra ID evaluates the conditions and logs what would have happened, without actually blocking or challenging anyone
The policy blocks all sign-ins immediately
The policy only applies to the break-glass account
questions.explain: Report-only mode lets Mara confirm the policy behaves correctly on real sign-ins before flipping it to enforced.
